Advaita Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Advaita Vedanta.question: All objects, all experiences, all matter, all consciousness, all awareness are somehow also this one fundamental reality _____

All objects, all experiences, all matter, all consciousness, all awareness are somehow also this one fundamental reality Brahman.

Advaita Vedanta.fact: While closely related to Samkhya, the Advaita Vedānta tradition rejects this dualism, instead stating that reality cannot evolve from an inert, consciousness- and intelligence-less principle or essence.

Advaita Vedanta.fact: First, how did Brahman, which is sat ('existence'), without any distinction, become manifold material universe? Prakasatmans (13th c.) defense of vivarta to explain the origin of the world, which declared phenomenal reality to be an illusion, became the dominant explanation, with which the primacy of Atman/Brahman can be maintained.

Advaita Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Advaita Vedanta.fact: Advaita also posits "the fourth", Turiya, which some describe as pure consciousness, the background that underlies and transcends these three common states of consciousness. Baal.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Baal.question: The _____ was Semitic title often used in reference to deities.
Baal.fact: Baal (), or Ba'al (), was a title and honorific meaning "owner" or "lord" in the Northwest Semitic languages spoken in the Levant during antiquity. Scholars previously associated the theonym with solar cults and with a variety of unrelated patron deities, but inscriptions have shown that the name Baal was particularly associated with the storm and fertility god Hadad and his local manifestations.
